Welcome to Malden Manor, where our aim is to provide an educational experience of the highest quality for all the children in our care. By creating an inclusive and stimulating learning environment, we seek to capture pupils’ interest, extend their knowledge and raise their aspirations. Our teaching and learning is designed to bring learning to life, both in the classroom and through a variety of inspiring experiences in the wider community. In line with our objective of being the best we can be, we encourage children to take an active role in their education, developing the skills they need for independent learning. Parental involvement is vital for children to achieve their best so it is encouraged at every stage of learning.
Malden Manor is a vibrant and welcoming community in which we strive for the highest standards of attainment – whether academic, artistic or sporting. We find and nurture hidden talents, celebrating the strengths of every child.
Our expectations in terms of both learning and behaviour are high and the children respond with delightful enthusiasm, politeness and consideration for others. Our broad curriculum and rich programme of extra-curricular activities – including the popular breakfast and after-school clubs – provide a well-rounded education, supported by excellent pastoral care. Together with my team of dedicated staff and governors, I invite you to visit the school to see for yourself the fantastic opportunities it offers your child.

By creating an inclusive and stimulating learning environment, we seek to capture pupils’ interest, extend their knowledge and raise their aspirations. Our teaching and learning is designed to bring learning to life, both in the classroom and through a variety of inspiring experiences in the wider community. In line with our objective of being the best we can be, we encourage children to take an active role in their education, developing the skills they need for independent learning. Parental involvement is vital for children to achieve their best so it is encouraged at every stage of learning.
Malden Manor is a vibrant and welcoming community in which we strive for the highest standards of attainment – whether academic, artistic or sporting. We find and nurture hidden talents, celebrating the strengths of every child.
Our expectations in terms of both learning and behaviour are high and the children respond with delightful enthusiasm, politeness and consideration for others. Our broad curriculum and rich programme of extra-curricular activities – including the popular breakfast and after-school clubs – provide a well-rounded education, supported by excellent pastoral care. Together with my team of dedicated staff and governors, I invite you to visit the school to see for yourself the fantastic opportunities it offers your child.
Wraparound Care
From January 26. Roar Kids Academy will be providing the Before School and After School Care at Malden Manor Primary & Nursery School.
Bookings must be made directly with Roar Kids Academy.
The below link takes you directly to their booking portal where you will be required to register a new account.
Please note the following points:
ALL questions asked in the registration must be answered fully in order to be activate your account.
None of the additional or emergency contact details can be the same
If you use Tax Free Childcare as a form of payment please remember to follow the steps and connect your government account to your Roar Kids Academy booking account.
Our system will automatically request the funds from your account. You DO NOT need to transfer any funds manually.
For all other forms of childcare vouchers, please select your provider from the list when checking out and then manually connect your provider to us so that we get paid.
The system automatically locks out bookings 24 hours in advance.
Whilst we encourage parents to book in advance so that we can prepare the correct food allocations, we do also accept ad hoc same day bookings at an additional admin cost of £2.50 per booking.
Please email info@roarkidsacademy.com to complete your booking. Also, rest assured we will never turn away a child so should it be so last minute that you weren’t able to contact us in time then please send your child to the wraparound as normal and we can always back date a payment.

Before School Care
Before School Care is open from 7:30 am to 8:45 am. There is a choice of breakfast which includes options such as cereals, croissants, yoghurt and fruit.
Please ensure your child is dropped off at least 15 mins before the session ends if you wish them to have breakfast
After School Care
After school care is open from 3:20pm to 6:00pm Each afternoon there is a planned play session led by one of our qualified play workers, and there are also plenty of games and themed activities to choose from. A hot meal is provided at 4:30pm
For both the 3:20pm - 6:00pm & 4:30pm - 6:00pm sessions, the flexible pick up is from 5:15pm only as we need time to seat the children properly for their hot meal. (Should you need to pick up your child at another time on an ad hoc basis then please do so by emailing

By creating an inclusive and stimulating learning environment, we seek to capture pupils’ interest, extend their knowledge and raise their aspirations. Our teaching and learning is designed to bring learning to life, both in the classroom and through a variety of inspiring experiences in the wider community. Together with my team of dedicated staff and governors, I invite you to visit the school to see for yourself the fantastic opportunities it offers your child.
5 Year Vision
Strategic 5 Year Vision
The governing body, alongside the SLT at Malden Manor have been developing a 5 year strategic vision. We have been thinking about what our aspirations are for the whole school community. We have based this vision around the school values (Achievement, High Standards, Happiness, Safety and Respect) and our mission statement:
“At Malden Manor we seek to instil a love of learning. Children learn that difference and diversity are valued and welcomed. We endeavour to offer an educational experience which develops the whole child and enables them to be the best that they can be. Our values are at the heart of all that we do and we aim to forge strong links with families and the wider community.”
The vision contains 3 key areas: High Quality Teaching and Learning, A range of quality experiences across the curriculum for pupils and Financial stability with improving grounds and premises
We will use this vision to develop and support the School Development Plan, which also contains a governance section. The vision and our strategic plan are working documents which will be reviewed and modified as necessary.

Our broad curriculum and rich programme of extra-curricular activities – including the popular breakfast and after-school clubs – provide a well-rounded education, supported by excellent pastoral care. Together with my team of dedicated staff and governors, I invite you to visit the school to see for yourself the fantastic opportunities it offers your child.
Our Shared Values
At Malden Manor Primary School, we take our responsibility to prepare children for life in modern Britain seriously. We ensure that fundamental British Values are introduced, discussed and lived through our ethos, shared values and unity of the school. High standards, achievement, happiness, respect and safety are our ideals that contribute to the development of our children. All curriculum areas provide an opportunity for furthering understanding of our values. In particular, lessons in RE, Humanities, SMSC (Spiritual, Moral, Social and Cultural) and PSHCE (Personal, Social, Health and Citizenship Education) provide excellent opportunities to deepen and develop this understanding.Our school makes extensive efforts to ensure our children have exposure to a wide and rich experience within and beyond their local community. Opportunities such as sporting events, visits to different places of worship and residential trips offer experiences children can hugely benefit from both during and beyond their primary school years.
The school teaches the British Values of Democracy, Rule of Law, Individual Liberty, Mutual Respect and Tolerance of those with different Faiths and Beliefs across the PSHCE and RE curriculum. Please click on the link below to see the additional opportunities we offer.

Governor Welcome
Rachel Lambert - Chair of Governors - LA Governor
Hello. I am Rachel Lambert. I am the Chair of the Governing Body.I took up this role in November 2020 after co-chairing for several months before this. I have been a governor of Malden Manor since 2014. My background is in education. I am a qualified secondary school teacher, with experience in Middle and Senior Leadership roles. I also have extensive knowledge of Early Years education from my time as a self-employed childminder. I am passionate about good quality, comprehensive, inclusive education - something that Malden Manor does very well.
It is a privilege to be the Chair of the Governing Body. I am very lucky to have a wonderful, dedicated group of governors, with varied backgrounds and a wealth of experience working alongside me and the school staff. Together we support the SLT in the strategic vision and development of the school.
Malden Manor is such a vibrant, welcoming and diverse school - it is a true reflection of the community in which we live. I still marvel at all the fantastic work going on to enable all our children to succeed and enjoy their time at school. As a parent who has had 2 children at the school, I have first hand knowledge of how children are effectively equipped for their next steps, how a love of learning is fostered and how proud pupils are to be part of the Malden Manor community.
Joseph Odiari - Vice Chair of Governors - Co-opted Governor
I am the Vice Chair of the School governing body and have been a Governor since 2016. I joined the Governing body as a way of giving something back to the local community of which I am a part. I am a civil servant by background and my children have attended the school, with my eldest having recently moved to High school.
With the pupils coming from diverse backgrounds, I am especially motivated to ensure that they can see a similar level of diversity and inclusivity on the school board that works for them.
I am passionate about Learning and am committed to working to ensure all our children get an excellent and well-rounded education. Literacy is a key area of personal interest and as an extracurricular activity, I have loved coming into the school to read to key stage 1 children and have them read to me.
Amy El-Borgi - Parent Governor
Hi, I’m Amy El-Borgi and I’ve been a parent Governor at Malden Manor since 2023. I am a member of the Finance, Premises and Personnel Committee and the link Governor for Early Years Reading/Phonics.
I have two daughters who’ve been at the school since nursery and are currently in Years 1 and 3. I work for an Academy Trust and previously worked for many years on education policy at the Department for Education.
I joined the Governing Body because I wanted to contribute to the school, and do what I can to support the school leadership to continue to provide the best possible educational opportunities for pupils.
Manikandan Nanappan - Co-opted Governor
I've been a co-opted governor at the school since September 2022, driven by my passion for education. I believe every child deserves a quality education, regardless of their background. My goal is to ensure all students have the best chance to succeed in school and life.
I've witnessed first-hand how education transforms lives and helps students overcome challenges. I'm committed to working with others to provide every child with opportunities to thrive.
With a background in asset management and exposure to diverse cultures, I aim to make a positive impact on students' lives. I'm excited to collaborate with the governing body to establish Malden Manor Primary and Nursery School as a high-quality institution where all students can flourish.
Adele Rowe - Co-opted Governor
I have been a co-opted Governor at Malden Manor since December 2018 once I had joined the Malden Manor as the School Business Manager. I firmly believe in great education for all and enabling the finances of the school to support the children to be the best they can be.
I was previously a parent governor for 8 years at my children's primary school which gave me a great insight to the role of a Governor and I realised it was one I wanted to pursue again.
I will remain a governor when I leave Malden Manor as School Business Manager at the end of June 2023. I am looking forward to still being able to support the school in the future.
Adam Hedley-Smith - Parent Governor
I was delighted to join the FGB in April 2019 as a Parent Governor. Having my daughter in Year 6 and my son in Year 2, I have a keen interest in all parts of our wonderful school and wanted to help and support in as many ways as possible.
My background in the commercial / corporate world of software and tech sales organisations means I hope to be useful in areas concerning data analysis, training, culture and values...I also love debates and asking lots of questions (just ask the SLT, I’m sure they’ll confirm this!)
I am very excited about working with the first-class staff team at the school - there is some amazing work being done with the kids at our school and within our local community - we must, and will, continue to nurture and develop that.
Outside of work and being a Governor, I am a sports addict, although that consists of mainly watching it rather than playing it nowadays. Rugby was my game when I was lad but in recent years Golf has become a passion. We moved to Worcester Park / Old Malden 6 years ago and as a family we love spending time with our friends and extended families and continue to enjoy making our home in the area.
Here’s to another challenging but successful year ahead for all involved with Malden Manor School. I look forward to getting to know more of the parent and staff community during 2023!
Kasia Weir - Community Governor
Hi, my name is Kasia Weir, I’ve been a governor at Malden Manor since March 2025, motivated by my passion for education and supporting children with special educational needs and disabilities. As a SEND teacher based in Chessington, I believe strongly in the importance of inclusivity and diversity, and I want to ensure that all children, regardless of their needs, have the chance to succeed.
Having lived in the area all my life, I am committed to making a positive difference in the community and to celebrating the strengths of every child. With a love for teaching, education, and the humanities, I am excited to contribute my experience to the governing body and to help Malden Manor continue to be a place where all students are supported to thrive.
Louise Dibble - Community Governor
As an ex-pupil of Malden Manor Primary School myself I am very excited to have become a Community Governor and look forward to being a part of the school’s future as well as its past. I worked as a Specialist Portage Practitioner for Achieving for Children for 16 years, working with pre-school children with SEND and their families, and am passionate about giving children the best possible support so they can reach their full potential. Due to my background in Early Years education, I am the link Governor for Early Years and Early Reading & Phonics and I am looking forward to coming into school to see the great work that is being done here. I hope to be able to contribute to the ongoing success of the school.
I have lived in Old Malden all my life and many of you will know me as one of the Group Lead Volunteers and the Beaver Team Lead at 1st Old Malden Scout Group. I also enjoy singing in a choir and hope that memorising all the words keeps my brain sharp!
Simon Pang - Community Governor
I am pleased to serve as a Community Governor at Malden Manor Primary and Nursery school and to support the education and wellbeing of pupils during these important early years. I joined the governing body because I believe that primary education lays the foundations not only for academic success, but also for confidence, curiosity, and a lifelong love of learning. I am also a member of the Finance, Premises and Personnel Committee.
I grew up in the area and went through the education system at local schools, so have had first hand experience of the impact that schools can have on young people. I have lived locally for over 30 years, I now have a family of my own and my children go to another local primary school, in years 2 and 5.
I have a background in strategy and consumer insight, specialising in understanding how to get more people in England physically active. It is a privilege to be part of the governing body, and I am committed to fulfilling this role with care, integrity, and a focus on what matters most: the happiness, progress, and development of every child in our school.
Eileen Bone has stepped down from the Board of Governors effective of the 28th February 2025.
Andy Fuller has stepped down from the Board of Governor effective of the 1st September 2025.

Welcome to Malden Manor, where our aim is to provide an educational experience of the highest quality for all the children in our care. By creating an inclusive and stimulating learning environment, we seek to capture pupils’ interest, extend their knowledge and raise their aspirations. Our teaching and learning is designed to bring learning to life, both in the classroom and through a variety of inspiring experiences in the wider community. In line with our objective of being the best we can be, we encourage children to take an active role in their education, developing the skills they need for independent learning. Parental involvement is vital for children to achieve their best so it is encouraged at every stage of learning.
Malden Manor is a vibrant and welcoming community in which we strive for the highest standards of attainment – whether academic, artistic or sporting. We find and nurture hidden talents, celebrating the strengths of every child.
Our expectations in terms of both learning and behaviour are high and the children respond with delightful enthusiasm, politeness and consideration for others. Our broad curriculum and rich programme of extra-curricular activities – including the popular breakfast and after-school clubs – provide a well-rounded education, supported by excellent pastoral care. Together with my team of dedicated staff and governors, I invite you to visit the school to see for yourself the fantastic opportunities it offers your child.

Welcome to Malden Manor, where our aim is to provide an educational experience of the highest quality for all the children in our care. By creating an inclusive and stimulating learning environment, we seek to capture pupils’ interest, extend their knowledge and raise their aspirations. Our teaching and learning is designed to bring learning to life, both in the classroom and through a variety of inspiring experiences in the wider community. In line with our objective of being the best we can be, we encourage children to take an active role in their education, developing the skills they need for independent learning. Parental involvement is vital for children to achieve their best so it is encouraged at every stage of learning.
Malden Manor is a vibrant and welcoming community in which we strive for the highest standards of attainment – whether academic, artistic or sporting. We find and nurture hidden talents, celebrating the strengths of every child.
Our expectations in terms of both learning and behaviour are high and the children respond with delightful enthusiasm, politeness and consideration for others. Our broad curriculum and rich programme of extra-curricular activities – including the popular breakfast and after-school clubs – provide a well-rounded education, supported by excellent pastoral care. Together with my team of dedicated staff and governors, I invite you to visit the school to see for yourself the fantastic opportunities it offers your child.

pageCache.text:
Welcome to Malden Manor, where our aim is to provide an educational experience of the highest quality for all the children in our care. By creating an inclusive and stimulating learning environment, we seek to capture pupils’ interest, extend their knowledge and raise their aspirations. Our teaching and learning is designed to bring learning to life, both in the classroom and through a variety of inspiring experiences in the wider community. In line with our objective of being the best we can be, we encourage children to take an active role in their education, developing the skills they need for independent learning. Parental involvement is vital for children to achieve their best so it is encouraged at every stage of learning.
Malden Manor is a vibrant and welcoming community in which we strive for the highest standards of attainment – whether academic, artistic or sporting. We find and nurture hidden talents, celebrating the strengths of every child.
Our expectations in terms of both learning and behaviour are high and the children respond with delightful enthusiasm, politeness and consideration for others. Our broad curriculum and rich programme of extra-curricular activities – including the popular breakfast and after-school clubs – provide a well-rounded education, supported by excellent pastoral care. Together with my team of dedicated staff and governors, I invite you to visit the school to see for yourself the fantastic opportunities it offers your child.
Finance, Premises & Personnel Committee
Malden Manor Primary and Nursery School Governing Body
Finance Premises and Personnel Committee (FPP) – Terms of Reference2025 -2026
To monitor progress on any key issues in the School Development Plan, Governors Development Plan and Risk Register which fall within the committee’s remit.
1) To determine and review financial policy including consideration of long-term planning and resourcing.2) In consultation with the Headteacher, to draft/recommend the annual budget spending plan to FGB, ensuring it is consistent with and supports the School Development Plan priorities.To advise and consult with the governing body on financial issues.To be familiar with the Local Authority budget spending plans, formula funding structure and policies for financial delegation.To monitor the school budget expenditure (including specific purpose grants) with reference to criteria for receipt of the grant and the annual spending plan. To make reports at least once a term to the governing body.To ensure that the school has the required Finance and GDPR policies, plus related Procedures, in place, and that these are communicated to all relevant staff.To authorise virements from one area of budget spending to another in order to respond to unexpected expenditure needs up to an agreed limit approved by the governing body.(See appendix 1 for Authorisation levels)To agree the level of delegation to the Headteacher for the day-to-day financial management of the schoolTo review the school’s charging and remission policy on an annual basis and make recommendations to the governing body.To monitor school fund expenditure and ensure the audit of school funds for presentation to the governing bodyTo receive and, where appropriate, respond to periodic audit reports. To agree a detailed action plan with evidence of regular monitoring where appropriate.To ensure that a register of business interests is maintained for all Governors, Senior Leadership Team and Finance Staff.To ensure the schools’ compliance with the DFE Schools Financial Values Standard. To review the documentation as required, agree an action plan and timetable for any remedial action.To review, monitor and approve the Governors Allowances scheme under delegation.To review benchmarking data on an annual basis. (SFVS)To monitor and review the three-year budget plan annually.
Premises, Grounds and Environment
1) To provide support and guidance for the Headteacher on all matters relating to the school premises and grounds, security, Health and Safety.2) Annually to ensure inspection of the premises and grounds and prepare a statement of priorities for maintenance and development linked to the School Development Plan to support delivery of a first-class curriculum.3) To propose and approve the costs and arrangements for maintenance, repairs and decoration within the budget allocation.4) To oversee the preparation of and to monitor premises services contracts (e.g. fuel/water, cleansing, grounds maintenance)5) To work in liaison with the Health and Safety Committee to ensure the school premises meet health and safety requirements. To receive termly reports from the Health and Safety Committee6) To ensure that governors’ responsibilities are discharged regarding litter under the Environmental Protection Act 1990.To review and approve the lettings and charging policy annually as delegated by the GB.To contribute towards an Accessibility Plan, with review every three years minimum.To consider how the use of the school premises may contribute to the development of Extended Schools.To ensure the school has an effective Risk Management strategy, including appropriate documented procedures, and regularly monitor and review the school’s compliance with those procedures.To ensure that there is relevant training and guidance for the Site Manager and/or key staff liaising with building contractors.To consider sustainability in relation to school premises, grounds maintenance and repairs, and when awarding contracts for school improvements and additional facilities.To ensure that an appropriate inventory is maintained and to approve the disposal of inventory items.To monitor and review the Emergency Plan annually.
To be aware of legal requirements and procedures relating to personnel issues.To ensure that all staffing policies and procedures contribute to achieving the best outcomes for children.To ensure the staffing structure, retention and succession planning is sufficiently flexible to deliver the School Development plan objectives.To review the Shadow Staffing Structure once a year.To monitor progress on any key issues in the School Development Plan, Governors Development Plan and Risk Register which fall within the Committee’s remit, at least termly.To monitor Continued Professional Development for all staff and its contribution to school improvement.To review annually the school’s Appraisal policies.To decide on procedures for staff appointments excluding Heads.To ensure that safe recruitment procedures are in place for all staff and volunteers working in the school, including those involved in extended school activities.To be involved in the development of all of the school’s policies relating to personnel matters, including:Staff consultationCode of conductPay (through the Pay Panel*)Discretionary Leave of absenceCapabilitySafeguarding and Child ProtectionRecruitment, Selection and Staff Retention plus Succession PlanningContinuing Professional Development and Appraisals.Discipline and GrievanceStaffing reduction proceduresEqualities Scheme/Policy, aspects related to Staff - liaise with CPPWhistleblowingGroup size of the school (to be reviewed at least once every three years)To approve, or recommend them for approval by the governing body, in line with the policies scheme of delegation and to ensure that systems are in place to make all staff aware of these policies.
To annually review the current staffing structure and workforce development plan.To draft criteria for the approval of the governing body about the use of discretionary elements of pay provisions and make recommendations about implementing them.To be consulted on and to approve job descriptions for the staff.To be responsible for reviewing the Headteacher’s job description should the need arise.To liaise with the finance committee in implementing the current School Development Plan in staffing matters.To ensure that all staff are able to maintain an appropriate Work-Life Balance
* To recommend a Pay Panel comprised of a minimum of three Governors, which includes the Chair of Governors and/or the Vice Chair of Governors. The Pay Panel will be appointed annually by FGB.
To monitor and review the allocated sections of the Risk Register termly and report back to the FGB.
Membership of Finance Premises and Personnel Committee
The HeadteacherSchool Business ManagerAt least four Governors of Malden Manor Primary School who are not members of staff (three present to form a quorum)
Frequency of Meetings: A minimum of one meeting per term.

pageCache.pageTitle: Key Stage 2 Curriculum Meeting - Years 3, 4, 5 & 6 3.30pm - Malden Manor
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Malden Manor, where our aim is to provide an educational experience of the highest quality for all the children in our care. By creating an inclusive and stimulating learning environment, we seek to capture pupils’ interest, extend their knowledge and raise their aspirations. Our teaching and learning is designed to bring learning to life, both in the classroom and through a variety of inspiring experiences in the wider community. In line with our objective of being the best we can be, we encourage children to take an active role in their education, developing the skills they need for independent learning. Parental involvement is vital for children to achieve their best so it is encouraged at every stage of learning.
Malden Manor is a vibrant and welcoming community in which we strive for the highest standards of attainment – whether academic, artistic or sporting. We find and nurture hidden talents, celebrating the strengths of every child.
Our expectations in terms of both learning and behaviour are high and the children respond with delightful enthusiasm, politeness and consideration for others. Our broad curriculum and rich programme of extra-curricular activities – including the popular breakfast and after-school clubs – provide a well-rounded education, supported by excellent pastoral care. Together with my team of dedicated staff and governors, I invite you to visit the school to see for yourself the fantastic opportunities it offers your child.

pageCache.text:
Welcome to Malden Manor, where our aim is to provide an educational experience of the highest quality for all the children in our care. By creating an inclusive and stimulating learning environment, we seek to capture pupils’ interest, extend their knowledge and raise their aspirations. Our teaching and learning is designed to bring learning to life, both in the classroom and through a variety of inspiring experiences in the wider community. In line with our objective of being the best we can be, we encourage children to take an active role in their education, developing the skills they need for independent learning. Parental involvement is vital for children to achieve their best so it is encouraged at every stage of learning.
Malden Manor is a vibrant and welcoming community in which we strive for the highest standards of attainment – whether academic, artistic or sporting. We find and nurture hidden talents, celebrating the strengths of every child.
Our expectations in terms of both learning and behaviour are high and the children respond with delightful enthusiasm, politeness and consideration for others. Our broad curriculum and rich programme of extra-curricular activities – including the popular breakfast and after-school clubs – provide a well-rounded education, supported by excellent pastoral care. Together with my team of dedicated staff and governors, I invite you to visit the school to see for yourself the fantastic opportunities it offers your child.
